description: Ground-truth defects deliberately planted in the sample PRD. Used to measure the agent's recall.

defects.defect: Schedule H/H1 drugs auto-dispensed from an AI-read prescription with no registered pharmacist verification.
LLM misreading a handwritten prescription (drug, strength or dose) directly triggers an order: no confidence threshold, no human review, patient-safety risk.
Prescription images and health data stored indefinitely and reused for model improvement and marketing without specific consent.
Health data sent to a third-party LLM API (possibly cross-border) with no processor agreement, retention or no-training terms stated.
Aadhaar number collected over WhatsApp and stored in the user profile; restricted use and storage rules for Aadhaar.
Phone number alone is the identity (FR7): SIM swap, number recycling or shared phones allow account takeover and access to health data and autopay.
UPI Autopay recurring debits with no pre-debit notification or per-order confirmation; amount can vary up to Rs 15,000.
Big-bang launch to all 2M users with no feature flag, staged rollout, kill switch or rollback plan.
Critical dependency (inventory availability API) is TBD and 'will be ready', and the timeline of ~4 weeks with 3 engineers is unrealistic.
Success metrics are unmeasurable: no baseline, target, timeframe or guardrail metrics.
Vague, untestable NFRs and accuracy bar ('fast', 'scalable', 'secure', 'real-time', 'accuracy should be high').
Target users are elderly Indian chronic patients but v1 is English only; no accessibility or confirmation step before automatic orders.
Refill date formula ignores dose changes, partial deliveries, discontinued drugs, prescription expiry and multiple prescriptions.
Caregivers can add up to 5 family members and their prescriptions with no proof of consent or relationship.
No monitoring, alerting or fallback when the WhatsApp BSP or LLM API is down or rate-limited; no capacity or cost analysis.
